classifications.VERIFIED FACT: An event, act or status that the cited source documents directly (for example, a signature, a launch or an appointment).
classifications.OFFICIAL TARGET: A quantified goal set by an official body. It is not an outcome and must not be read as achieved.
classifications.ANNOUNCED PLAN: A programme, institution or product an official body has announced or presented, whose operational delivery the registry has not verified.
classifications.INDEPENDENT ANALYSIS: An inference drawn by TheMoroccoAI from two or more records. It is labelled as interpretation, not as fact.
classifications.UNVERIFIED CLAIM: A statement attributed to a source whose underlying data the registry has not independently checked.

records.source_organization: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)

records.verification_note: A 510(k) "substantially equivalent" decision is a US market clearance, which the FDA distinguishes from premarket approval (PMA). It is not a clinical-outcome finding and says nothing about authorisation or use in Morocco. The record names no Moroccan entity: its association with the Morocco-based DeepEcho rests on the matching name and device type, the deepecho.io e-mail domain and Moroccan data sites in the 510(k) summary (MAI-EV-0039), UM6P Ventures' 2023 statement that the startup was preparing an FDA submission (MAI-EV-0028) and the Moroccan government's statement (MAI-EV-0033). No source establishes the legal relationship between the applicant and a Moroccan company. Excerpts match the page's visible text.

records.title: Ministry of Health convention with DeepEcho on AI prenatal ultrasound in public facilities
records.source_organization: Maroc.ma (national portal of the Kingdom of Morocco)
records.claim: At GITEX Future Health Africa Morocco in May 2026, the Ministry of Health and Social Protection signed a partnership convention with DeepEcho setting up an institutional and research framework for the dissemination, adoption and clinical evaluation of AI solutions for pregnancy-monitoring ultrasound in public health facilities. The source describes a progressive deployment, within an evaluative scientific study, in primary-care establishments and local hospitals, of a Moroccan solution that it says obtained the "approbation" of the US Food and Drug Administration.
source_excerpts: le ministère a signé une convention de partenariat avec la société "DeepEcho", visant la mise en place d’un cadre institutionnel et de recherche pour la diffusion, l’adoption et l’évaluation clinique de solutions d’IA dans le domaine de l’échographie de suivi de la grossesse au sein des établissements de santé publics

à travers le déploiement progressif, dans le cadre d’une étude scientifique évaluative, d’une solution numérique marocaine innovante, ayant obtenu l’approbation de la Food and Drug Administration Américaine (FDA), au niveau des établissements de soins de santé primaires et des hôpitaux de proximité
records.verification_note: The verified fact is the signature and the stated framework. The progressive deployment is described as the convention's purpose; no source retrieved shows that the evaluative study or any deployment in a public facility has started. The article's "approbation" is inaccurate as regulatory terminology: the FDA record (MAI-EV-0032, MAI-EV-0039) is a 510(k) clearance, and a US clearance does not authorise clinical use in Morocco. The article does not name the device.

records.title: TOUBKAL: peer-reviewed description of the system and its reported workloads
records.source_organization: The Journal of Supercomputing (Springer)
records.claim: A peer-reviewed article in The Journal of Supercomputing, by authors affiliated with Mohammed VI Polytechnic University's College of Computing, describes Toubkal's GPU partitions (NVIDIA A100 nodes from the initial 2022 deployment and H100 nodes added in 2025). It states that fine-tuning of transformer-based large language models and large-scale computational fluid dynamics simulations have been run on the system, and presents as a benchmark the fine-tuning runs that produced the GemMaroc Moroccan Darija language models, which it attributes to "Belkasmi et al." while citing the GemMaroc preprint by Skiredj et al.
source_excerpts: TOUBKAL: a high-performance supercomputer powering scientific research in Africa
The initial deployment in 2022 included five Dell XE8545 nodes with dual AMD EPYC 7713 CPUs and four NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB GPUs per node.
In 2025, three Dell XE8640 nodes were added, each with dual Intel Xeon Platinum 8468 CPUs and four NVIDIA H100-HBM3-80GB GPUs.

we examine practical workloads such as fine-tuning transformer-based large language models (LLMs) and conducting large-scale computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, both of which have been successfully run on Toubkal.
we present a practical benchmark demonstrating the fine-tuning of a large language model (LLM) performed on the Toubkal supercomputer by Belkasmi et al.
This work led to the creation of GemMaroc
records.verification_note: Open-access article (CC BY 4.0), published online 3 October 2025. Every author lists an affiliation with the university that hosts and runs Toubkal, so the workload statement is the operator's own report, peer-reviewed but not independent. It documents specific fine-tuning runs, not the scale, share or continuity of AI use. The article names their authors "Belkasmi et al.", but its reference [57] is the GemMaroc preprint by Skiredj, Azhari, Atou, Tazi and Berrada (MAI-EV-0042); that preprint does not itself say where the runs were made. The article's statement that they ran on Toubkal comes from its own authors, none of whom is an author of the preprint. The article's user counts and utilisation figures are not recorded. Benchmark, accuracy and energy figures in the article are not recorded. The verified fact is what the article states. Excerpts were matched against the article page retrieved on the retrieval date; automated requests to the publisher can receive a bot-challenge page, which the source checker reports as blocked and does not bypass.

records.title: GemMaroc: the preprint describing the GemMaroc fine-tuning runs
records.source_organization: arXiv (preprint by Skiredj, Azhari, Atou, Tazi and Berrada)
records.claim: The preprint introducing the GemMaroc Moroccan Darija language models, by three authors from Mohammed VI Polytechnic University's College of Computing, one from Hugging Face and one from the National Institute of Posts and Telecoms, reports that its fine-tuning experiments ran on two NVIDIA A100-80GB GPUs, and the 27-billion-parameter GemMaroc model on eight NVIDIA H100-80GB GPUs, taking about 48 GPU-hours. It expresses the total cost as a cloud cost, using a public on-demand rate in a Runpod Cloud region, and does not name the computing facility used.
source_excerpts: College of Computing, Mohammed VI Polytechnic University, Benguerir, Morocco
All fine-tuning experiments were conducted on 2×A100-80GB GPUs, except for our largest model, the 27-billion-parameter GEMMAROC, which was fine-tuned on 8×H100-80GB GPUs.
consuming approximately 48 GPU-hours and keeping the total cloud cost well under $100.
Based on the public on-demand rate of $2 per A100-hour in the selected Runpod Cloud region.
records.verification_note: arXiv preprint, version 1 of 20 May 2025, not peer-reviewed; excerpts matched against the PDF. The excerpt on the hardware was checked against the rendered page: the PDF's text layer splits the small-capital model name and drops the hyphen in "H100-80GB" at a line break, so automated matching reports it missing. No author is named Belkasmi: the Toubkal article (MAI-EV-0041) attributes these runs to "Belkasmi et al." but its reference [57] is this preprint by Skiredj et al. The preprint does not mention Toubkal, the African Supercomputing Centre or any acknowledgement of computing resources; its cost footnote uses a commercial cloud provider's public rate, which may be a costing convention rather than where the runs took place. It therefore neither confirms nor rules out that the runs were made on Toubkal. Three of the five authors are affiliated with the university that runs Toubkal.

records.title: GeneLM: genomic language model trained on the Toubkal supercomputer
records.source_organization: Briefings in Bioinformatics (Oxford University Press); Akotenou and El Allali
records.claim: A peer-reviewed article by two researchers of Mohammed VI Polytechnic University's College of Computing reports that the coding-sequence classification experiments for their bacterial genomic language model were conducted on the Toubkal supercomputer, with training on two NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs for a total of 37 hours over two epochs.
source_excerpts: The CDS classification experiments were conducted on the Toubkal supercomputer.
The training was performed on two NVIDIA A100 GPUs, each equipped with 80GB of memory.
the total training duration was 37 h for two epochs.
providing access to the supercomputing resources (cc.um6p.ma/toubkal-super-computer)
records.verification_note: Open-access article (CC BY), published 3 July 2025. The publisher's site refuses automated requests, so the excerpts were matched against the full text deposited in Europe PMC (PMC12222049). Both authors are affiliated with the university that runs Toubkal: this is the researchers' own account of one training run, not independent documentation, and it says nothing of Toubkal's overall AI use, its scale or its continuity.

records.title: Ministry release: memorandum signed on the Nexus AI Factory platform
records.source_organization: Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform (mmsp.gov.ma)
records.claim: The ministry's own news release states that, on the sidelines of GITEX Africa Morocco 2026, Nexus Core Systems, the Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform, the Ministry of Investment, Convergence and Evaluation of Public Policies, and the Moroccan Agency for Investment and Export Development (AMDIE) signed a memorandum of understanding on the "Nexus AI Factory Plateform" project, described as combining a high-performance computing data centre, a centre of excellence and an innovation hub.
source_excerpts: En marge de GITEX Africa Morocco 2026, Nexus Core Systems, le Ministère de la Transition Numérique et de la Réforme de l’Administration, le Ministère de l’Investissement, de la Convergence et de l’Evaluation des Politiques Publiques et l’Agence Marocaine de Développement des Investissement et des Exporattions (AMDIE) ont signé un protocole d'accord (MoU) marquant le lancement opérationnel des premières phases du projet « Nexus AI Factory Plateform».

Le projet repose sur une montée en puissance technologique soutenue par un investissement initial de 12 milliards de dirhams mobilisé sur deux phases qui visent la création de 125 emplois directs fin 2027
Phase 1 – Hub de Nouaceur : Une enveloppe de 5 milliards de dirhams sera consacrée à l'activation d'une capacité de 16 MW sur le site de Nouaceur.
Ce déploiement portera la capacité cumulée à 36 MW fin 2027.
records.verification_note: Release by a signatory, dated 8 April 2026; the verified fact is the signature of the memorandum. Despite the words "lancement opérationnel", the phase investment, capacity and job figures are stated in the future tense, as commitments. The release describes the MAD 12 billion as an "investissement initial" "mobilisé sur deux phases"; that wording does not establish that any amount has been spent, and the release documents no expenditure. Nothing in the release shows construction or operation. Spellings are as printed ("Plateform", "Exporattions"). The other two signatories (the investment ministry and AMDIE) are not entities in this registry. The release does not reproduce the memorandum, and this registry has not obtained its text.

records.title: Ministry release: general assemblies of four JAZARI institutes
records.source_organization: Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform (mmsp.gov.ma)
records.claim: The ministry's release states that the general assemblies of four JAZARI institutes, JAZARI ROOT, the JAZARI institute for education and technological innovation, JAZARI Industrie X.0 and the JAZARI institute for smart cities, were held in Rabat on Tuesday 8 September 2026, chaired by the Minister Delegate for Digital Transition and Administration Reform, after the publication in August 2026 of the decisions approving their founding conventions.
source_excerpts: Les assemblées générales de quatre Instituts « JAZARI » se sont tenues ce mardi à Rabat, sous la présidence de Madame Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni, ministre déléguée auprès du Chef du Gouvernement, chargée de la Transition numérique et de la Réforme de l’administration.
